angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 523,166 km at 36.55 pc = 0.19 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 27.3578 +/- 0.0125 mas (same row, RUWE 1.00): 36.55 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.752 +/- 0.014 solar radii from Campante et al. 2015, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of Kepler-444 e in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015ApJ...799..170C/abstract): 523,166 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.758 +/- 0.043 solar masses from Campante et al. 2015, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of Kepler-444 e in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015ApJ...799..170C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5046 +/- 74 K from Campante et al. 2015, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-444 e in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015ApJ...799..170C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Campante et al. 2015, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-444 e in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015ApJ...799..170C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/kepler-444.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.565, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
